A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPIRAL study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite title, numbering, and layout changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original LiDAR generation benchmarks, inference ablations, segmentation robustness analyses, and supervised and semi-supervised data-augmentation results.

after.justification: V2 retains original generation and segmentation experiments and additionally reports adverse-weather evaluations and closed-loop switching statistics.

M1.justification: The U-Net architecture, training losses, EMA semantic predictions, confidence-triggered feedback, and semi-supervised training procedure remain unchanged. Replacing conditional/unconditional 'modes' with 'steps' clarifies terminology without changing the algorithm.

E1.justification: V2 adds the fog and wet-ground subsets of Robo3D as out-of-distribution segmentation tests using generated-data augmentation (Table 3). This extends coverage to two adverse-weather conditions while retaining the SemanticKITTI and nuScenes generation and segmentation tasks.

E2.justification: The main benchmark comparator set is retained. However, the appendix jittering comparison drops the R2DM combinations with RangeNet++, SPVCNN++, and RangeViT, retaining only LiDARGen combinations (v1 Table 5 versus v2 Table 6).

E3.justification: V2 adds a switching-point study using 1,000 samples per dataset at 256 denoising steps and extends augmentation evaluation to weather-corrupted inputs using the existing 1%, 10%, and 20% labeled-data settings. Existing splits, preprocessing, training budgets, and generation metrics remain unchanged; revised baseline scores do not establish that those protocols changed.

E4.justification: V2 substantially extends the analysis with adverse-weather robustness tests and an empirical study of when semantic feedback activates. It also extends the efficiency comparison with 128-step timing and removes the R2DM portion of the jittering analysis. The existing NFE and confidence-threshold ablations remain.

E5.justification: V2 introduces plus/minus reporting for average switching steps: 180 +/- 36 on SemanticKITTI and 189 +/- 39 on nuScenes, using 1,000 samples each. The meaning of the plus/minus quantities is unspecified. Neither version reports multi-seed uncertainty for the main benchmark scores.

E6.justification: Table 1 substantially revises baseline results under unchanged stated settings: S-FPD changes from 1787.91 to 1366.17 for LiDARGen+SPVCNN++, 986.87 to 522.47 for LiDM+SPVCNN++, and 218.80 to 363.16 for R2DM+RangeNet++. Comparative rankings and reported margins consequently change. V2 also adds weather, switching-point, and 128-step timing results and removes R2DM jittering results. SPIRAL's main benchmark scores, nuScenes Table 2, and augmentation Tables 7-9 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1-15 retain the same objectives, EMA update, semantic feature construction, distance definitions, kernel, and depth transformation. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive mathematical revision appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: joint depth/reflectance/semantic generation, semantic-aware evaluation, strong performance with a compact model, and useful segmentation augmentation. Adding 'and Understanding' to the title does not introduce a new scientific capability.

C2.justification: V2 narrows the explanation of SPVCNN++ underperformance to LiDARGen and LiDM outputs. It newly interprets late switching as avoiding unstable early predictions and weather results as robustness without weather-specific fine-tuning. The efficiency discussion adds the 128-step speed-quality tradeoff; the limitations section is substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a SPIRAL project-page link and Robo3D access and license information. Architecture, preprocessing, optimizer, training hardware, and existing implementation disclosures are retained; the PDFs do not establish a change in the underlying implementation.

R1.justification: V2 adds nine cited works, including La La LiDAR, SEALION, a 3D/4D world-modeling survey, and generative augmentation for object point-cloud segmentation. These expand supporting context without substantially rewriting the related-work discussion or redefining novelty.

P1.justification: V2 revises the title, distinguishes inference modes from conditional/unconditional steps, edits several explanatory passages, and moves the efficiency discussion from the appendix into Section 4.3. Most prose and the overall argument remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds a front-page visual teaser, redraws the pipeline, architecture, and metric diagrams, and adds an explicit mode-switching panel. It revises plots, expands the augmentation table, and relocates and restructures the timing table. Table 4 also changes scale headers from negative to positive exponents while retaining the numerical entries, creating inconsistent scaling notation.

improvement.justification: The weather tests and switching-point analysis strengthen validation of downstream robustness and the feedback mechanism, while clearer diagrams improve explanation of the unchanged method. These gains are limited by unexplained baseline-score revisions, removal of the R2DM jittering evidence, and inconsistent Table 4 scale labels. The revision modestly improves the paper overall without establishing better SPIRAL benchmark performance.
